result.answer:
Verdict: NOT ENOUGH EVIDENCE

Evidence for: The paper does compare a multimodal MNER model against text-only NER models, reporting that the proposed MNER model with modality attention "significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art text-only NER models" by using visual contexts [S:21bdf776ac68#2]. The SnapCaptions dataset labels entities as PER, LOC, ORG, and MISC, so a location-versus-person comparison is possible in principle [S:21bdf776ac68#4].

Evidence against / limitation: No supplied span reports per-entity-type performance or separate gains for locations versus people; the specific claim that the improvement was greater for locations than for people is therefore not addressed by the provided evidence [S:21bdf776ac68#2][S:21bdf776ac68#4].

claims.text: The proposed MNER model with modality attention significantly outperforms state-of-the-art text-only NER models by leveraging visual contexts.
claims.note: Span states the MNER model with modality attention significantly outperforms state-of-the-art text-only NER models by leveraging visual contexts.

claims.text: The SnapCaptions dataset labels named entities with the types PER, LOC, ORG, and MISC.
claims.note: Span states SnapCaptions named entities in captions are manually labeled with entity types PER, LOC, ORG, MISC.

citations.text:

citations.title: Multimodal Named Entity Recognition for Short Social Media Posts
citations.text:
The SnapCaptions dataset is composed of 10K user-generated image (snap) and textual caption pairs
where named entities in captions are manually labeled by expert human annotators (entity types: PER,
LOC, ORG, MISC). These captions are collected exclusively from snaps submitted to public and
crowd-sourced stories (aka Snapchat Live Stories or Our Stories). Examples of such public
crowd-sourced stories are “New York Story” or “Thanksgiving Story”, which comprise snaps that are
aggregated for various public events, venues, etc. All snaps were posted between year 2016 and 2017,
and do not contain raw images or other associated information (only textual captions and obfuscated
visual descriptor features extracted from the pre-trained InceptionNet are available). We split the dataset
into train (70%), validation (15%), and test sets (15%). The captions data have average length of 30.7
